summary: At v45 step 84, the confirmed Sunsword hit reaches uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_msg_lightobj, but JavaScript only records note_unported and omits the radiance message. C uses the saved lit-artifact name, target visibility, and corporeal/form guards to print the source-ordered feedback before poison and kill messages. The prior v33 reach attempt fled before this helper; this admitted v45 case reaches it after the hit pager.

source.branch: uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_do_hit sets hmd.lightobj when a lit light artifact hits a monster that hates light. After the hit and silver messages, hmon_hitmon calls this helper when that flag is set. A visible target with saved_oname gets “<saved name>’s radiance penetrates deep into”; a visible target without it gets “The light sears”; an unseen target is capitalized and gets “is seared”. Append “ flesh” when the target is neither noncorporeal nor amorphous. The obj argument is unused. The helper writes one pline and consumes no RNG or game state.
callers: C producer: uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_do_hit:1038–1040 sets hmd.lightobj for a lit artifact-light object and a light-hating target; js/uhitm.js:hmon_hitmon_do_hit:2821 already mirrors that flag.

C caller: uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon:1880–1881 invokes hmon_hitmon_msg_lightobj after hmon_hitmon_msg_silver and before poison/kill feedback; js/uhitm.js:hmon_hitmon:3760–3761 currently records note_unported at the same position.

Runtime route: cmd.c:rhack force-fight input F, hack.c movement attack dispatch, uhitm.c:do_attack:448 -> hitum:758 -> hmon:819 -> hmon_hitmon:1754 -> hmon_hitmon_msg_lightobj:1702. The JavaScript path is cmd.js force-fight dispatch -> hack.js attack dispatch -> uhitm.js do_attack -> hitum -> hmon -> hmon_hitmon.
dependencies: The helper reuses the existing JS owners for mon_nam, canspotmon, highc, noncorporeal, amorphous, and s_suffix; no dependency needs a new random or state effect.

C mon_nam, canspotmon, highc, noncorporeal, amorphous, and s_suffix preserve source evaluation order. C concatenates the final “ flesh” suffix only after the visibility-dependent target text is selected.

evidence: Read the complete source helper uhitm.c:1702–1727. It initializes mon_nam before branching, chooses the visible/invisible format, conditionally appends the target’s flesh suffix, and emits exactly one pline. obj is explicitly UNUSED; the helper has no RNG or state mutation.

Read uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_do_hit:1038–1040 and hmon_hitmon:1877–1881. The helper runs only after the hit has set hmd.lightobj, after silver feedback, and before poison/kill feedback. The current JS caller at js/uhitm.js:3760–3761 has the corresponding named gap.

Saved admitted v45 C-first recording challenges/cases/v45/v45-hmon-hit-lightobj-sunsword-gremlin-attempt7-cfirst.session.json has input F at zero-based step 83, a confirmed Sunsword hit on the gremlin at step 84, and a space at step 85 that reveals “Sunsword’s radiance penetrates deep into the gremlin’s flesh!”. The selected evaluation reports the first screen mismatch at step 84 with matched RNG through that boundary.

The closest earlier record, investigations/synthetic/v33/v33-sunsword-light-sears.json, reached a fleeing boundary at step 53 in monmove.c:distfleeck before hmon_hitmon_msg_lightobj. It did not provide runtime evidence for this helper; the v45 C-first forced-hit case is a distinct successful-hit path.
